summary: The candidate captures every paper-internal core result and foundational definition represented in the Gold artifact, including Lemma 3.7, Theorems 3.8, 3.14, 3.15, Corollary 3.19, Lemma 4.5, and Theorem 4.7. Most formulas and hypotheses are faithful and the LaTeX is well formed. The principal deficiencies are the complete omission of four externally attributed background results, a mathematically significant replacement of isotopy by homotopy in Lemma 4.5, misclassification of Corollary 3.19 as a theorem, incomplete standalone specification of the Hochschild relation, and several duplicate entries.
strengths: All eight paper-internal claim entries in the Gold reference have recognizable candidate counterparts.
The main target, Theorem 3.8, is stated accurately with the relative tensor product, glued four-manifold, and bimodule categories preserved.
The self-gluing, capping, trisection, and three-manifold gluing formulas retain their essential hypotheses and conclusions.

All six Gold foundational definitions are covered, and the candidate additionally extracts useful nearby definitions such as lasagna fillings, the skein lasagna module, self-gluing, and surface modules.
Lemma and theorem numbering is generally recoverable from IDs or titles, page locators are supplied, and displayed formulas have balanced delimiters.
issues: None of the four Gold background entries is extracted or externally attributed: Morrison–Walker–Wedrich skein lasagna theory, the Ren–Willis surjective gluing map, Banyaga's fragmentation lemma, and Gay–Kirby trisection existence and stable uniqueness.
The candidate states Lemma 4.5 for homotopic links (彼此同伦), whereas the Gold statement requires isotopic links (彼此同痕); these are not interchangeable conditions.
Corollary 3.19 is assigned type "theorem" instead of "corollary".
The zero-th Hochschild homology definition names the quotient relation sim_2 but does not state the defining relation f_*(a) sim_2 f^*(a), reducing its standalone precision.
The cornered four-manifold bimodule is duplicated in two nearly identical entries, and the surface-module tensor product is likewise duplicated.
An abstract-level copy of the four-manifold gluing theorem duplicates Theorem 3.8 without its numbered label, adding avoidable redundancy.
The three-manifold category entry appears to reverse the roles of T and T' in the displayed boundary for a morphism from T to T', making its convention unclear.

entryLevelComparison.notes: Theorem 3.8 is mathematically faithful, but an additional abstract-level entry duplicates it.
The quotient-to-glued-module map and isomorphism conclusion are preserved.
The Hochschild homology and punctured self-glued manifold formula is accurate.
The theorem and the generators of the third equivalence relation are both represented.
The formula is faithful, but the extraction type is theorem rather than corollary.
The candidate changes the required isotopy condition to homotopy.
The boundary orientations, glued manifold, and relative tensor-product conclusion are retained.
All Gold external/background claims are absent, so their attribution and role in the proofs are lost.
